newsitem.title: UK: International LPG up on US demand, CP expectations.
newsitem.headline: International LPG up on US demand, CP expectations.

text.p: Worldwide prices for Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) continued to firm in the week ending August 30 as U.S. demand and anticipation of stronger Saudi Contract Prices pushed up the market.

The Saudi Contract Price (CP), the benchmark against which most Middle Eastern sales of LPG are priced, is due to be released on Saturday, although a spokeswoman for Saudi Petroleum Overseas Ltd told Reuters they may not appear until Sunday.
Given the strength of demand from the United States, traders expect the CP to rise.
One estimated that the propane price would be $170 a tonne, with another putting propane at $180 and butane at parity or even higher.

Spot Mideast Gulf prices have risen as a result, with FOB prices now seen at a premium to CP. There were rumours that a small propane cargo of less than 7,000 tonnes was traded at CP +1 FOB Ras Tanura during the week.
Trade in the Middle East was stifled by the uncertainty surrounding CP levels.
"Everybody's waiting for the CP and watching the U.S. All eyes are now on the U.S." said a trader.
He added that buyers from East Asia have started to buy at higher prices because they see bullish signals from the U.S., encouraging them to cover before the price starts to jump.

A Korean buyer was heard buying a mixed cargo of 20,000 tonnes each of propane and butane at CP +24 C+F Ulsan, for loading and delivery in September. And this equates to CP +26 C+F Japan, according to a trader.
But demand into Japan remains subdued with storage levels still very high, according to traders.

European prices were kept up by the strength in the United States. Both butane and propane strengthened there over the week, boosted by a butane pipeline explosion near Dallas last weekend and by API data showing low propane inventories.
This provided a floor for European LPG. One trader said "not all companies have the logistics to take cargoes transatlantic, but some do and could solve an imbalance like this".
Propane moved at $203 a tonne CIF Flushing for 10,000 tonnes for September delivery on Friday, the seller told Reuters. This followed trade at $197 CIF Flushing earlier in the week.

While large cargoes firmed, small seagoing coasters were up sharply. "Now that we're entering winter, demand is increasing for small spot cargoes," said one trader. "Demand is not necessarily for large cargoes, but for specific sizes. As a result, local cargoes can be sold FOB at CIF prices".
One seller reported receiving a bid for a propane coaster at $195 a tonne FOB Teesside, and was indicating an offer at $198 a tonne in reply.

But butane was not so strong. There were rumours of a trade at $177 a tonne FOB UK South Coast, and following the closure of a Moroccan butane tender prices were seen coming under some pressure in Europe.

The Moroccan tender was awarded on Thursday, in two lots. A Mediterranean producer reported selling 40,000 tonnes at a fixed price of between $216 and $220 a tonne CIF Morocco, with another 12,000 tonnes heard awarded to a trader.

Butane was heard traded earlier in the week at $205 CIF Lavera for 4,000 toonnes, while propane was reported at $195 CIF Lavera for 7,000 tonnes, off a mixed propane/butane vessel sold into Spain. Trade was relatively thin in the Mediterranean with storage still near tanktops in the Lavera region.
